Published online:
    September 7, 2026

Geographic focus:
    United States

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — references August jobs data and Jackson Hole speech
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — Sep 15-16 Fed meeting, Dec hike forecast
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    UBS revised its Fed outlook, now forecasting two 25bp rate hikes in September and December 2026, reversing its prior no-change call. The pivot is driven by a strong August jobs print (162K jobs added, unemployment steady at 4.1%), hawkish signals from Fed Chair Warsh at Jackson Hole, and rising inflation risks from supply bottlenecks. Citi and Macquarie also revised forecasts. Markets are pricing a ~58% probability of a September hike, up from 52% the prior day.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES (core focus is US interest rate trajectory driven by labor market and Fed communication)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 95 (dominant theme — UBS, Citi, and Macquarie all revising toward hikes)
Probability of increase: 58% (per CME FedWatch for September meeting)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 10 (only briefly referenced via Waller's conditional hold stance)
Probability of holding: 42% (implied residual from CME FedWatch)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 0 (not mentioned, no cut scenario discussed)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 80 (Distinctly more hawkish — strong jobs data, hawkish Fed Chair rhetoric, and coordinated broker forecast revisions all pointing toward imminent hikes; market pricing also shifted hawkish intraday)
